tools.description: Use for how much money households in Poland hold and where: cash, bank deposits, bonds, shares, investment funds, insurance and pension savings, the share outside cash and deposits, and Poland against OECD countries. Give NBP (via the ECB) and OECD as sources and the quarter or year. Financial assets of households in Poland at the end of each quarter since 2003 from the quarterly financial accounts compiled by NBP and published by the ECB (QSA): total, cash, deposits, debt securities, equity, investment funds, life insurance, pension entitlements and other, in PLN billion with shares and year-on-year change; finwire_household_invested_share (Udział oszczędności pracujących finwire: share of financial assets outside cash and deposits, i.e. debt securities, equity and funds, insurance and pension entitlements); Poland among countries in the OECD financial dashboard (share of currency and deposits with rank, equity, funds, pension; net financial worth per person in USD PPP); investment funds, PPK, IKE and IKZE and retail savings bond sales from other finwire datasets.

quarters.description: Number of past quarters in the summary, default 8.

tools.name: get_poland_forecasts
tools.description: Use for forecasts of GDP growth, inflation, unemployment, deficit and public debt of Poland for this and next year from the European Commission, OECD and NBP, how forecasts changed and which institution was most accurate. Say which institution and edition each number comes from and that these are forecasts, not finwire.pl advice. For the next CPI reading or RPP decision, use get_nowcast. Latest edition of every institution with forecasts of real GDP growth, annual average inflation (European Commission: HICP; NBP, OECD and Finwire Nowcast: CPI), unemployment (LFS), general government balance and debt as % of GDP for the current and next years, the previous edition, outturns, mean forecast errors of each institution (forecasts made a year earlier) and the finwire index finwire_forecast_accuracy. Every edition is stored separately (European Commission since spring 2011). Finwire Konsensus is included only for indicators where it beat the best single institution in the backtest. Optional year selects the target year in the summary.

year.description: Target year in the summary; default the year after the latest European Commission edition.

tools.name: get_world_comparison
tools.description: Use for Poland against other countries: central bank rates and the NBP rate rank, real house prices abroad, price to income or rent, credit gap, and whether Polish housing is overvalued (Finwire Housecast). Say that a forecast is a model estimate. Poland against other countries from the BIS (Bank for International Settlements) and the OECD. topic policy_rates: central bank policy rates of BIS economies, the place of the NBP rate (finwire_policy_rate_rank, 1 = highest rate) nominal and real (rate minus annual CPI inflation), median, rank history, real effective exchange rate of the zloty. topic house_prices: real and nominal annual change of residential property prices by country with the place of Poland, and price-to-income and price-to-rent ratios of Poland and the OECD average. topic credit_cycle: credit-to-GDP gap of Poland and the debt service ratio of the private non-financial sector (no household-only ratio for Poland). topic housecast: Finwire Housecast (finwire_housing_valuation_gap), the housing valuation gap of Poland and panel countries and the model forecast of real house prices 4 and 8 quarters ahead; a horizon below the accuracy gate has no numbers.

country.description: Country code (ISO 3166 alpha-2, euro area = XM) to show next to Poland in policy_rates and house_prices.

tools.name: get_oecd_comparison
tools.description: Use to compare Polish pensions (replacement rate) or labour taxes (tax wedge) with OECD countries, also countries outside the EU such as the United States, the United Kingdom or Japan. For the tax wedge in EU countries, use get_eu_earnings. For a pension forecast by birth year, use get_pension_forecast. OECD comparative data. Pension replacement rates from Pensions at a Glance: first pension as % of individual earnings before retirement, net and gross, men and women, average wage, full career from age 22, mandatory schemes, for Poland, the OECD average and every country of the OECD comparison, with the rank of Poland and finwire_oecd_pension_gap (Poland minus the OECD average, percentage points). Tax wedge from Taxing Wages: income tax plus employee and employer social contributions as % of total labour costs for six household profiles in every OECD country (also outside the EU: United States, United Kingdom, Japan, Canada, Switzerland, Norway), history of Poland and the OECD average since 2000, and finwire_oecd_tax_wedge_gap. For the tax wedge in EU countries from Eurostat use get_eu_earnings. For a pension forecast for a birth cohort use get_pension_forecast.

topic.description: pension (replacement rates) or tax-wedge; default both.

profile.description: Tax wedge household profile, default single_100 (single person without children, average wage).

tools.name: get_new_companies
tools.description: Use for how many new companies (sp. z o.o., S.A., partnerships) are registered in KRS each month and for all new firms in Poland together with sole proprietorships. For closures and suspensions of sole proprietorships, use get_business_registrations. New commercial companies entered in the Polish National Court Register (KRS) each month by legal form (limited liability, simple joint-stock, joint-stock, partnerships), counted by finwire.pl from the Ministry of Justice KRS API (daily bulletin and current extracts), with applications to register a sole proprietorship in CEIDG (MRiT) for the same month, the share of companies among new firms, the current month so far against the same days a year earlier and the finwire index finwire_new_companies_pulse (new sole proprietorships plus new companies, % year on year).

history.description: Number of past months in the summary, default 12.

tools.name: get_tourism_pressure
tools.description: Use for tourism in a Polish municipality, county or province: bed places per 1000 residents, nights spent, tourists, bed occupancy by month, and where short-term rental pressure is highest. Presja turystyczna finwire (finwire_tourism_pressure) from Statistics Poland (GUS BDL): bed places in tourist accommodation on 31 July per 1000 residents for Poland and each municipality with its rank; nights spent and tourists per year (Poland, provinces, counties, nights per resident), nights and bed occupancy rate per month (Poland, provinces). With q: municipalities matching the name, with the county nights per resident. GUS has no nights for municipalities after 2014.

q.description: Part of a municipality name, e.g. Zakopane; omit for Poland, provinces and the top municipalities.

tools.name: get_pension_systems
tools.description: Use to compare the average ZUS pension with the average KRUS farmer pension, by year and province. For the latest monthly ZUS pension, use get_pension_stats. Average monthly gross old-age pension from ZUS and average pension and disability benefit of farmers from KRUS (GUS BDL; KRUS figure covers both): yearly since 1999 for Poland and 16 provinces, the latest year-to-date period with the previous year, gap in PLN and KRUS as % of ZUS. For the latest monthly ZUS pension, use get_pension_stats.

tools.name: get_us_economy
tools.description: Use for the US economy: US inflation (CPI), the US jobs report, US unemployment, real wages in the USA, US Treasury yields and an inverted yield curve, and US national debt. For Polish data, use get_macro_indicator. For other countries, use get_world_comparison. US economy from official US sources. topic inflation: CPI y/y and m/m and core CPI (BLS) with Polish CPI (GUS) for the same month. topic labor: BLS jobs report, change of nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate, average hourly earnings and Realne płace w USA finwire (finwire_us_real_wage_growth, wage growth minus CPI, pp). topic yields: US Treasury par yield curve now and a year earlier, 10Y-2Y and 10Y-3M spreads, days with an inverted curve in the last 365 days. topic debt: US public debt (Debt to the Penny) and Licznik długu USA finwire (finwire_us_debt_per_second, debt growth per second in USD and PLN at the NBP mid rate). Default all topics. Each value has its period. No forecasts.

history.description: Number of past months in the summary of one topic, default 6; ignored for all.

tools.name: get_car_costs
tools.description: Use for the cost of driving a car in Poland: cost of 100 km or of a trip with petrol, diesel, LPG or an electric car, taxes when buying a used car or importing a car (PCC, customs duty, excise, import VAT), toll motorways and speeding fines. For maximum fuel prices only, use get_fuel_prices; for charging prices by network, use get_ev_charging_prices. Daily cost of driving 100 km in Poland (finwire_car_cost_100km) with petrol 95, diesel, LPG and electricity (home G12 tariff, public AC and DC chargers) for an average compact car (ICCT real-world consumption), with the prices of the day and their sources. Optional distance_km gives the cost of a trip for the chosen energy, consumption and persons. Also the legal constants of buying a car: PCC on a used car from a private person (rate, exemption threshold), customs duty for cars from outside the EU (third-country duty, 0% for cars originating in the USA since the EU regulation), import VAT and the order duty, excise, VAT; toll motorway sections free or paid for cars up to 3.5 t with announced changes; speeding fines and penalty points. No amounts for concession tolls.

distance_km.description: Trip distance in km for the trip cost.

energy.description: Fuel or charging for the trip cost, default petrol95.

consumption.description: Consumption per 100 km (litres, or kWh for ev_*); default the reference car.

persons.description: Persons sharing the trip cost, default 1.

round_trip.description: Count the way back too, default false.

tools.name: get_ofe_stats
tools.description: Use for open pension funds (OFE) in Poland: members, net assets, accounting unit value by fund, OFE rates of return over 1, 3, 5 and 10 years, and how 100 PLN in OFE compares with the ZUS subaccount. For IKE and IKZE, use get_ike_ikze_stats. For a pension forecast, use get_pension_forecast. Polish open pension funds (OFE) from KNF. topic market: latest month (members, net assets, weighted average accounting unit value, contributions from ZUS) with the previous month and a year earlier, and each fund (unit value, change in 12 months, share of net assets). topic returns: net rates of return over 12, 36, 60 and 120 months by fund and weighted average (KNF, April and October) and 100 PLN in OFE vs 100 PLN on the ZUS subaccount over the same window (yearly subaccount indexation from 1 June), with Różnica OFE i subkonta ZUS finwire (finwire_ofe_vs_subaccount_10y, pp). Default all topics. Past results, no forecasts, not investment advice.

fund.description: Optional fund id or part of the name (e.g. "pzu", "nationale-nederlanden") for the 100 PLN comparison; default weighted average of all OFE.

tools.name: get_build_cost
tools.description: Use for how much it costs to build a house in Poland, the cost of building 1 m2 in a voivodeship, the official replacement cost indicator (koszt odtworzenia 1 m2) announced by voivodes, and how construction prices change (GUS). For flat prices, use get_housing_prices; for BGK price limits of the family housing loan, use get_rkm_price_limits. What building a house costs in Poland according to official indicators. Replacement cost of 1 m2 of a residential building announced by each voivode every half year (average of the two latest announcements, derived from BGK family housing loan limits): voivodeship city, the municipalities bordering it and the other municipalities of the voivodeship. Gives a 120 m2 house per voivodeship and its change in a year, Koszt budowy domu finwire (finwire_house_build_cost: a 120 m2 house at the middle value of the 16 voivodeships), an optional estimate for your floor area, and GUS construction and assembly price indices (m/m and y/y, construction of buildings and other divisions). The replacement cost is an official indicator, not a contractor quote: a real house can cost more or less depending on the project, standard and materials, and the plot is not included.

voivodeship.description: Voivodeship slug, name or voivodeship city, e.g. malopolskie or Kraków; default all 16.

area_m2.description: Usable floor area of the house in m2 for an estimate (needs voivodeship).

location.description: Part of the voivodeship for the estimate: rest = other municipalities (default), neighbors = municipalities bordering the voivodeship city, city = the voivodeship city.

history.description: Number of past months of GUS construction prices in the summary, default 6.

tools.name: get_cumulative_inflation
tools.description: Use for cumulative inflation in Poland: how much prices rose in total from one year or month to another, e.g. since 2020 or from 2022 to 2026. For the latest monthly CPI reading, use get_macro_indicator. For the purchasing power of an amount, give the cumulative inflation from this tool. How much consumer prices in Poland rose in total between two months or years, from the chain of GUS consumer price indices since 1982: December on December for full years (as in the GUS yearly table) and month-on-month indices within a year. "From 2022" means from January 2022; "to 2026" means to December or to the latest published month. Gives the cumulative inflation in %, how many times prices rose, the average per year and the number of months. Without from: cumulative inflation from the start of each recent year to the latest month and the December-on-December inflation of recent years.

from.description: Start: YYYY (from January) or YYYY-MM, e.g. 2022 or 2023-05.

to.description: End: YYYY (to December or the latest month) or YYYY-MM; default the latest published month.

years.description: Number of recent years in the summary tables, default 10.

tools.name: plan_parental_leave
tools.description: Use for maternity, parental and paternity leave in Poland: the dates of each leave from the birth date, how to split parental leave between the mother and the father, the maternity benefit (zasiłek macierzyński) per month and in total from gross pay, 81.5% or 100% and 70%, deadlines, and the weeks a parent loses. For 800 plus, Aktywny Rodzic and family allowance, use get_family_benefits. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Plan maternity, parental and paternity leave for both parents in Poland from the birth date (or the expected date), with the rules in force now. Order: maternity leave of the mother (20 weeks for one child), then her parental leave, then the father's parental leave (41 weeks for both parents, 43 for multiple births; each parent has 9 non-transferable weeks), paternity leave of up to 2 weeks from the birth. Gives the dates of each period, the split of weeks, the day the mother returns to work, and, when you give the gross pay, the maternity benefit per period, per month and in total. Gives both payment variants: 81.5% for the whole leave on the mother's request within 21 days after the birth (the father's 9 weeks always 70%), or 100% for maternity and paternity leave and 70% for parental leave. Gives the deadlines (81.5% request, paternity leave until the child is 12 months old, parental leave until the end of the year the child turns 6, notice 21 days before parental leave) and the non-transferable weeks that a parent loses. The benefit is never below the parental allowance (świadczenie rodzicielskie). A calculation, not a ZUS decision.

birth_date.description: Birth date or expected birth date, YYYY-MM-DD; default today.

children.description: Children from one birth (5 = five or more), default 1.

prenatal_weeks.description: Weeks of maternity leave before the birth, default 0.

mother_parental_weeks.description: Mother's parental leave weeks, with her 9 non-transferable weeks; default 32 (all she can take when the father takes his 9).

father_parental_weeks.description: Father's parental leave weeks, with his 9 non-transferable weeks; default 9. Weeks below 9 are lost.

paternity_weeks.description: Paternity leave weeks from the birth date, default 2.

mother_gross.description: Mother's average gross monthly pay of the last 12 months in PLN. Without it: no amounts for the mother.

father_gross.description: Father's average gross monthly pay of the last 12 months in PLN. Without it: no amounts for the father.

request_815.description: Mother's request for 81.5% within 21 days after the birth; default true. The result also gives the family total of the other variant.

tools.name: get_fuel_retail_estimate
tools.description: Use for what fuel will cost at Polish stations tomorrow (petrol 95, diesel) and how wholesale prices pass into pump prices. For the legally set maximum price and crude oil, use get_fuel_prices; for prices in other EU countries, use get_eu_fuel_prices. finwire estimate of the average pump price of petrol 95 and diesel in Poland for the next day (finwire_hurtcast_pb95, finwire_hurtcast_diesel): wholesale price of the last days plus the typical station margin measured on European Commission Weekly Oil Bulletin prices, plus VAT, not above the maximum price of the Minister of Energy while it applies. Each estimate has its date, VAT rate, maximum price and backtest accuracy (mean absolute error per litre over up to 104 weeks, share of weeks within 10 groszy). It is a prediction of the national average, not the price at a given station. For the legally set maximum price, use get_fuel_prices; for prices in other EU countries, use get_eu_fuel_prices.

weeks.description: Number of recent backtest weeks (estimate vs station average) in the summary, default 4.

tools.name: get_currency_forecast
tools.description: Use for where the euro, dollar, pound, franc or another currency may be against PLN in the next days, weeks or months, and for a range or table of the expected rate. For current and past NBP rates, use get_currency_rates. Do not present the range as a recommendation to buy or sell. finwire forecast of the NBP mid rate of a currency against PLN (Finwire FXcast) for the next NBP table, 1 week, 1, 3, 6 and 12 months: 80% and 50% ranges, the point ("no change" unless the forward rate won the 10-year backtest) and the forward rate from the central bank rate difference. Each horizon has backtest accuracy: share of forecasts with the actual rate inside the 80% range and mean error of "no change" and of the forward rate. Only horizons that passed the accuracy gate are given. 12 currencies: EUR, USD, CHF, GBP, NOK, SEK, DKK, CZK, HUF, JPY, CAD, AUD. It is a model range, not a rate quote and not investment advice. For current and past NBP rates, use get_currency_rates.

currency.description: Currency code, e.g. EUR, USD, GBP, CHF, NOK. Default: EUR, USD, GBP, CHF and NOK.

horizon.description: One horizon; default all published horizons.

tools.name: calc_net_income
tools.description: Use for take-home pay from an employment, mandate or work contract or B2B self-employment. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Monthly take-home pay in Poland from: employment contract (uop: umowa o pracę, standard costs, PIT-2 filed, no reliefs), mandate contract (zlecenie: ZUS, health, 20% costs, PIT-2), contract for specific work (dzielo: no ZUS, 20% costs) or B2B self-employment of a sole proprietor (b2b: tax scale, flat-rate tax (liniowy) or lump-sum ryczałt on revenue, chosen ZUS scheme). Returns social security (ZUS), health contribution, income tax, net, yearly totals, effective rate and, for uop and zlecenie, the cost to the payer. Rates of the Polish tax year, switching on 1 January. For one person choosing between business forms use compare_business_forms.

form.description: Form of work: uop employment, zlecenie mandate, dzielo specific work, b2b self-employment.

monthly_amount.description: PLN per month: gross pay (uop, zlecenie), contract amount (dzielo) or net revenue without VAT (b2b).

monthly_costs.description: b2b: monthly business costs, PLN net.

tax.description: b2b: tax form, default liniowy (flat-rate PIT).

lump_sum_rate.description: b2b ryczalt: rate in percent for the activity, e.g. 12 for IT services.

zus.description: b2b: social security scheme, default pelny (full).

ppk.description: uop: employee saves in PPK (workplace pension), default false.

student_under_26.description: zlecenie: pupil or student under 26 (no ZUS, no PIT).

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

tools.name: calc_employer_cost
tools.description: Use for the cost of an employee to the employer. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Total monthly cost to the employer of an employment contract (umowa o pracę) or a mandate contract (umowa zlecenie) in Poland for a given gross pay: employer pension and disability contributions, accident insurance (basic rate for payers up to 9 insured), Labour Fund (FP), Guaranteed Employee Benefits Fund (FGŚP), optional PPK, plus what the employee takes home. Rates of the Polish tax year.

ppk.description: uop: employee in PPK, default false.

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

tools.name: compare_mandate_vs_employment
tools.description: Use for mandate contract (umowa zlecenia) vs employment contract for the same gross pay: net, cost, paid leave, sick pay, notice and length of employment. For take-home pay of one form only, use calc_net_income. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Compare a mandate contract (umowa zlecenia, civil-law contract) with an employment contract (umowa o pracę) in Poland for the same monthly gross pay: take-home pay, social security (ZUS), health contribution, income tax, cost to the payer, statutory paid leave days and their value at a fixed salary, sick pay for a number of days and who pays it (employer sick pay at 80% after a 30-day waiting period vs ZUS sickness benefit only with voluntary sickness insurance and after a 90-day waiting period), notice period (Labour Code by tenure vs termination at any time under art. 746 of the Civil Code) and whether mandate periods count towards length of employment (art. 302^1 of the Labour Code, from the dates the law applies). Rates of the Polish tax year, switching on 1 January. Each rule comes from a verified fact; use get_business_guide with topic contracts for the legal texts.

monthly_gross.description: Monthly gross pay, PLN, the same on both contracts.

voluntary_sickness.description: Mandate: the contractor pays voluntary sickness insurance, default true (without it there is no sickness benefit).

student_under_26.description: Mandate: pupil or student under 26 (no ZUS, no PIT, no sickness benefit).

sick_days.description: Days of sick leave to compare, default 10 (up to the 33 days paid by the employer).

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

tools.name: compare_business_forms
tools.description: Use to compare a sole proprietorship (JDG) with a limited company (sp. z o.o.) by taxes and net income to the owner. For a shareholder resident abroad, give the dividend rate from get_tax_treaty. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Compare yearly taxes and net income to the owner for running a business in Poland as a sole proprietorship (JDG: tax scale, flat-rate tax (liniowy), lump-sum ryczałt) or a limited liability company (sp. z o.o.) with one shareholder (shareholder pays ZUS and the health contribution) or with two or more shareholders. Company profit taxed with CIT (reduced small-taxpayer rate when revenue fits the EUR limit at the NBP rate set by law, otherwise the standard rate; the rate used is in citRate) and the dividend tax: Polish statutory rate by default, or pass dividend_tax_rate from a tax treaty for a shareholder resident abroad. Assumes all profit is paid out as dividend. Not covered here: who may open which form (residence status), management board pay, Estonian CIT.

yearly_revenue.description: Yearly net revenue without VAT, PLN.

lump_sum_rate.description: Ryczałt rate for the activity in percent, default 12.

zus.description: JDG social security scheme, default pelny.

dividend_tax_rate.description: Dividend tax rate as a fraction, e.g. 0.05, for a shareholder resident in a treaty country.

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

tools.name: calc_zus_contributions
tools.description: Use for the social security contributions of a sole proprietor. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. Monthly social security contributions (ZUS: pension, disability, sickness, accident, Labour Fund) of a sole proprietor (JDG) in Poland under each scheme: start relief (ulga na start), preferential ZUS and full ZUS, with the contribution base. The health contribution depends on the tax form and income; use calc_net_income with form b2b for it.

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

tools.name: calc_notice_period
tools.description: Use for the end date of an employment contract in Poland after notice or by mutual agreement, the notice period, the last payday, the holiday equivalent, job search days and severance pay. Give the inputs and the assumptions with the result. The result is a calculation from statutory rates. It is not advice. End of an employment contract (umowa o pracę) in Poland under the Labour Code (Kodeks pracy) when the employee or the employer gives notice, or by mutual agreement (porozumienie stron): notice period from the length of service with this employer (2 weeks, 1 month, 3 months; trial contracts 3 working days, 1 week, 2 weeks), termination date (weekly periods end on Saturday, monthly on the last day of a month; a fixed-term contract ends earlier on its own end date), last payday, pay-out date of the holiday equivalent and its amount from gross pay and unused leave days, paid days off to look for a job when the employer gives notice, severance pay in months of pay with the cap, and the employment certificate day. Facts carry the act, article, link and verification date.

served.description: Day the notice reached the other party, or day of the agreement, YYYY-MM-DD.

by.description: Who ends the contract, default employee.

contract.description: Contract type: indefinite term, fixed term, replacement of an absent employee (fixed term), trial. Default indefinite.

start.description: First day of work for this employer, YYYY-MM-DD; include mandate or B2B work for the same employer.

trial.description: Trial contract: agreed trial length, default 3-months.

contract_end.description: Fixed-term, replacement or trial contract: end date written in the contract.

employer_reasons.description: Dismissal for reasons not related to the employee by an employer with at least 20 staff (gives severance pay).

payday.description: Payday in the company; 1-10 pays the previous month. Default 10.

monthly_gross.description: Gross monthly pay PLN, for the holiday equivalent amount.

unused_leave_days.description: Unused annual leave days, for the holiday equivalent amount.

tools.name: plan_business_entry
tools.description: Use when a person from abroad wants to start a business in Poland: available forms, taxes per form, steps and deadlines. Give the legal basis and the verification date of each fact. One call for someone from abroad starting a business in Poland: every legal form with available yes/no and the reason for their residence status, yearly taxes and net income to the owner for each available form (dividend tax at the tax-treaty rate of the owner country), setup steps, residence and identity requirements, and the deadline calendar for the form with the highest net income at these inputs. Facts carry the act, article, link and verification date.

owner_status.description: eu-eea: EU/EEA citizen; swiss: Swiss citizen; third-country-equal: non-EU national with permanent residence, EU long-term residence, a listed temporary residence permit, refugee or temporary protection status, Pole's Card or EU family member; third-country-other: other non-EU national (visa, visa-free, residence permit for running a business); foreign-company-eu-eea / foreign-company-other: a company seated abroad.

owner_country.description: Tax residence of the owner, ISO2 (e.g. DE, US); omit if Polish resident.

yearly_revenue.description: Expected yearly net revenue without VAT, PLN.

yearly_costs.description: Expected yearly business costs, PLN net.

vat_payer.description: Will be an active VAT payer (monthly).

lump_sum_rate.description: Ryczałt rate for the activity in percent, default 12.

year.description: Polish tax year; default the current one.

tools.name: get_business_forms
tools.description: Use to find which business forms a foreigner or a foreign company can use, and why. Give the legal basis and the verification date of each fact. All Polish business forms (sole proprietorship JDG, unregistered activity, sp. z o.o., P.S.A., S.A., general, limited and professional partnerships, branch, representative office) with available yes/no for the owner status, the reason, conditions (e.g. PESEL for CEIDG) and facts on capital, liability, registration and tax, each with the legal basis.

owner_status.description: eu-eea: EU/EEA citizen; swiss: Swiss citizen; third-country-equal: non-EU national with permanent residence, EU long-term residence, a listed temporary residence permit, refugee or temporary protection status, Pole's Card or EU family member; third-country-other: other non-EU national (visa, visa-free, residence permit for running a business); foreign-company-eu-eea / foreign-company-other: a company seated abroad.

tools.name: get_tax_treaty
tools.description: Use for tax on dividends, interest or royalties paid abroad. Also use for the countries that invest the most in Poland (NBP data). Give the legal basis and the verification date of each fact. Polish withholding tax on dividends, interest and royalties paid to a resident of a country: the statutory rate, the rate in the double tax treaty with Poland (portfolio and qualified holding), whether MLI modifies the treaty, and the EU/EEA/Swiss parent-subsidiary exemption with its holding conditions. Covers the largest investor countries by NBP data; without country returns the list and the ranking.

country.description: ISO2 code, e.g. DE, NL, US.

tools.name: get_compliance_calendar
tools.description: Use for the yearly tax, ZUS, VAT and reporting deadlines of a business. Calendar of tax, ZUS, VAT, payroll and reporting deadlines for a calendar year: monthly PIT/CIT advances or ryczałt, own ZUS, JPK_V7M, PIT and ZUS of employees, PPK, annual returns, annual health contribution, CIT-8, financial statements and JPK files. Dates are computed from statutory rules with the shift to the next working day; event-based duties (CRBR, ZUS registration, invoices) are listed as facts.

form.description: Business form: sole proprietorship on tax scale, flat-rate tax (liniowy) or lump-sum ryczałt, or limited company.

vat_payer.description: Active VAT payer (monthly JPK_V7M), default false.

year.description: Calendar year, default the current one.

tools.name: get_business_guide
tools.description: Use for company tax regimes and reliefs (CIT, Estonian CIT, IP Box, R&D relief, Polish Investment Zone). Also use for VAT, residence permits, PESEL, e-signature, hiring foreigners, labour law, accounting and closing a business. Give the legal basis and the verification date of each fact. Verified facts about doing business in Poland, each with the act, article, link to the official text and the verification date. Topics: intl-tax (selling into Poland from abroad, VAT registration, reverse charge, OSS, permanent establishment, transfer pricing, Estonian CIT, IP Box), residence (permits, MOS), identity (PESEL, NIP, trusted profile, e-signature), documents (sworn translation, apostille), forms, setup (steps and deadlines), activity (PKD 2025, regulated activities), wht, treaty, tax-residence, health (NFZ, A1), property (buying property as a foreigner), contracts, labour (Labour Code rules), hiring-foreigners (work permits, declarations), deadlines, accounting (books, invoices, KSeF, whitelist), incentives (Polish Investment Zone, regional aid map, R&D relief), exit (suspension, conversion, liquidation). Pass a topic, a query, or both.

topic.description: Guide section, see the tool description.

query.description: Words in English or Polish, e.g. "PESEL", "work permit", "likwidacja".

tools.name: get_business_glossary
tools.description: Use for the meaning of Polish business, tax and ZUS terms. Polish-English glossary of business, tax, ZUS and registration terms (JDG, sp. z o.o., CEIDG, KRS, ryczałt, KPiR, KSeF, JPK, CRBR, UPO, PSI and others) with one-line explanations.
